encounters.cc: husband reports patient has been acting strangely with irritability and insomnia

lines: Husband reports patient has been acting strangely with irritability and insomnia

This 46-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, history of primary central nervous system lymphoma, avascular necrosis of the right femoral head, and status post splenectomy two months prior for atraumatic rupture, presents to the Psychiatry clinic with her husband, who reports that she has been "acting strangely" for the past two weeks.
She was started on high-dose prednisone therapy for a severe lupus flare 1 month ago.
The husband describes her as being increasingly irritable, having difficulty sleeping, and expressing grandiose ideas.
She has also been spending large amounts of money online, which is uncharacteristic of her usual behavior.
She denies any history of similar symptoms in the past.
- Secondary Hyperaldosteronism due to Dietary Sodium Restriction (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Avascular necrosis of right femoral head
- History of primary central nervous system lymphoma
